verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: The new `if (err instanceof NotReadyError) throw err;` lets a transient "charge not settled yet" error propagate to poller.ts:13, which calls `gw.submit(charge.payload)` — but gateway.ts:3 documents submit() as NOT idempotent, so every tick resubmits a charge the gateway already holds and creates a duplicate charge. WHY: A charge that is merely still settling gets charged/submitted again on each poll tick, producing duplicate charges (the doc comment in errors.ts:1 says NotReadyError means "the gateway has the charge but has not settled it yet", which contradicts poller.ts:7's assumption that it means "the gateway never received it"). HOW: only resubmit when the gateway genuinely never received the charge — distinguish "never received" from "not settled" (e.g. a separate NotReceivedError / a `received` flag on NotReadyError) and for a merely-not-ready charge return a `pending`/retry-later state instead of calling gw.submit, or pass a provider-side idempotency key to submit.
verificationEvidence.rationale: Confirmed. errors.ts:1 defines NotReadyError as 'The gateway has the charge but has not settled it yet (transient)', and status.ts:8-10 now propagates it unchanged to poller.ts. poller.ts:7 documents the opposite assumption ('the gateway never received it: resubmit') and poller.ts:13-14 calls gw.submit on any NotReadyError. gateway.ts:3 documents submit() as NOT idempotent ('every call creates a new charge'). So a merely-still-settling charge is resubmitted on every poll tick, creating duplicate charges. The trigger is concrete and reachable, not speculative. This is also a different problem from the round-a-propagate entry (which was about misclassifying a transient error as terminal) — here the consequence is duplicate charges caused by propagating NotReadyError into the resubmit path, so it is not a repeat.

verificationEvidence.rationale: Confirmed: normalizeLocale does input.replace('_','-').split('-') and dereferences parts[1].toUpperCase() unconditionally. checkProfileFields only checks typeof patch.locale === 'string', then calls normalizeLocale. updateProfile passes the raw client body via sanitizeProfileUpdate. A request body {"locale":"en"} (a plain string with no separator) yields parts=["en"], parts[1] undefined, throwing TypeError on .toUpperCase() before any HttpError(400) — an unhandled 500. The failure path is reachable and the root cause is factually correct. This is a different problem from the existing denylist-sanitizer decision (which is about which fields pass through, not the locale normalization crash).

delivered.text: Because `normalizeLocale` assumes the input contains a `-` and dereferences `parts[1].toUpperCase()` at line 13, while `updateProfile` passes the raw client body to `checkProfileFields` with `locale` only type-checked as a string, a request like `POST { "locale": "en" }` makes `parts[1]` undefined and throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toUpperCase')`, returning an unhandled 500 instead of a validation error. Guard the split result in `normalizeLocale` and treat a missing region as unsupported by throwing `HttpError` with status 400 and the message `unsupported locale ${input}`.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: normalizeLocale accesses parts[1].toUpperCase() without guarding that a separator exists, so an input with no '-' or '_' (e.g. locale = "english" or "xx") makes parts[1] undefined and throws a TypeError. WHY: checkProfileFields calls normalizeLocale before the SUPPORTED_LOCALES check, so a member sending a single-token locale crashes the handler with an uncaught TypeError (HTTP 500) instead of returning the intended 400 'unsupported locale'. HOW: guard the missing segment, e.g. const [lang = '', region = ''] = input.replace('_', '-').split('-'); return region ? `${lang.toLowerCase()}-${region.toUpperCase()}` : lang.toLowerCase();
verificationEvidence.rationale: Confirmed: line 12-13 does `input.replace('_', '-').split('-')` and unconditionally calls `parts[1].toUpperCase()`. For a single-token input like "english" or "xx", split('-') yields a one-element array, parts[1] is undefined, and `.toUpperCase()` throws TypeError. checkProfileFields (line 39-41) calls normalizeLocale(patch.locale) before the SUPPORTED_LOCALES check, so a single-token locale crashes with an uncaught TypeError (HTTP 500) instead of the intended 400. Root cause and failure path are accurate; no upstream guard exists. Not covered by any previous decision.

HOW: reject non-string values instead of skipping them, e.g. `if (patch.displayName !== undefined && typeof patch.displayName !== 'string') throw new HttpError(400, 'displayName must be a string');` and likewise for bio/avatarUrl/locale.
